newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: British Telecom to study Singapore opening.
newsitem.headline: British Telecom to study Singapore opening.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc (BT) said on Monday it would study the potential impact on its own plans of Singapore's decision to allow new firms to compete with telephone monopoly Singapore Telecom from 2000.
"Obviously we will evaluate the impact," BT spokesman Martin O'Connor told Reuters.

"We can't at present discuss any impact today's announcement will have on our current and future plans in Singapore. However, we welcome the announcement, as BT believes very strongly that appropriate deregulation and the competition that it brings is good both for a country's economy as well as all customers."

BT is one of a small number of foreign telecommunications companies strongly tipped by analysts to try to take advantage of the deregulation of Singapore's basic telecommunications industry which will take place on April 1, 2000.

Communications Minister Mah Bow Tan said earlier on Monday Singapore would allow at least one, and possibly two, new operators to provide an integrated telecommunications service, including domestic and international telephone calls.
Foreign companies would be allowed to take up to a 49 percent stake in the new telecoms ventures with local companies holding the balance, he said.

Industry sources say such an investment in the Singapore market would fit very well with BT's avowed strategy of using joint ventures and alliances as a way of opening up new markets around the world.
Over the last three years, BT has invested several billion dollars in such investments, giving it large minority holdings in second carriers in several countries.
In 1993, BT invested US$4.3 billion in the United States' second largest long-distance telephone company, MCI Communications Corp, for a 20 percent stake.
It has also bought a 25 percent stake of New Zealand's second carrier Clear Communications Ltd as well as stakes in Korean and Japanese telecommunications companies.
